skill.name: affinity
skill.description: Search and maintain local contacts, identities, relationships, events, commitments, and recurring dates. Use when recording relationship evidence or reviewing a social CRM.
skill.summary: Manage contacts, relationship history, and follow-ups in a local CRM.
skill.author: ghostpawjs

security_audit.summary: Both installers execute unverified code from a moving branch, and the npm fallback can run an unpinned package. Most recon and backtick alerts match ordinary documentation; the writable-root setup and access to sensitive CRM records remain real concerns. No evidence of intentional exfiltration or an embedded prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Installers execute unverified remote scripts, and the npm fallback is unpinned.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before installation. Pin releases and npm versions, verify trusted signatures or checksums, and separate download from execution.

remediation.issue: Setup documentation suggests adding a persistent Codex writable root.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the database in a dedicated workspace directory. Require operator approval for external access and limit it to that directory for one session.

remediation.issue: An omitted contact selector makes export include the whole database.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit contact for normal exports. Gate whole-database export behind separate user approval and keep exports out of shared logs.

remediation.issue: Archived message text can enter agent context through journal review.
remediation.suggestion: Use summaries by default and label verbatim imports as untrusted data. Never use instructions from retrieved records to authorize tool calls or disclosure.

remediation.issue: A tool argument can override a do-not-contact restriction for a record.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user authorization for each override and log its reason. Never treat a CRM override as consent to send a message.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Contact Selector Expands Export Scope
semantic_findings.description: An export without a contact selector returns the whole CRM database instead of failing. An incomplete agent call could expose unrelated records in tool output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly documents the whole-database default. No external upload destination or automatic disclosure was found.

semantic_findings.title: Imported Messages Can Carry Indirect Prompt Injection
semantic_findings.description: Historical imports preserve original message text, and journal review can return it verbatim to an agent. Retrieved text could contain instructions that try to redirect the agent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The import and review paths are explicit. The reviewed guidance does not mark retrieved text as untrusted, but no embedded attack was found.

semantic_findings.title: Do-Not-Contact Override Lacks Documented User Approval

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both tool references expose the override as an input. The documented effect is on CRM records; there is no evidence that the tool sends messages.

content.value_statement: Scattered notes make it hard to remember past conversations and outstanding promises. Affinity keeps contacts, relationship history, commitments, and recurring dates in one local CRM.
actual_capabilities: Search and inspect contacts by name, email, handle, or other stored identity.
Record interactions, observations, milestones, and transactions with dates and participants.
Track promises and agreements through resolution, and review open commitments and upcoming recurring dates.
Review relationship timelines, maintenance priorities, and graphs that distinguish structural ties from social links.
Review duplicate contacts and merge confirmed matches into a chosen surviving record.
Import documented history in batches and use external references to avoid duplicate events on retries.
limitations: Requires a compatible Affinity CLI or local MCP connection and access to a SQLite database.
The documented shell and PowerShell installers run unverified remote code.
Recurring dates appear in review views; the skill does not send reminders or schedule outreach.
Relationship scores reflect recorded evidence and do not establish trust, closeness, or consent.

use_cases.title: Review client commitments
use_cases.description: Review open promises and upcoming renewals before a client check-in. Use the contact journal to confirm what was agreed.

use_cases.title: Clean up a contact database
use_cases.description: Compare duplicate candidates using stored identities and history. Confirm which record should remain before merging.

use_cases.title: Track coaching follow-through
use_cases.description: Record agent coaching conversations and agreed changes. Resolve each promise after checking the outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Find a contact
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: look up one record without changing it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the contact that matches [email or handle]. Report the matching name and ask me to clarify if more than one record is plausible.

prompt_templates.title: Review the coming week
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: prepare for a weekly review.
prompt_templates.prompt: List overdue and upcoming commitments for the next seven days. Show yearly dates in a separate list. Do not change any records.

prompt_templates.title: Log a conversation and a promise
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: capture an interaction and a separate obligation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [contact] using [known identity]. Record the conversation on [date] from [summary]. Create a separate promise for [action] due [date] without marking it kept.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a historical import
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a batch migration before writing to the live database.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [authorized archive] and propose a batch import without writing anything. Match contacts by stable identities and preserve external references for documented events. Flag unclear dates or identity conflicts. Seed known relationships without inventing events.

output_examples.input: Show overdue commitments and recurring dates for the next seven days.
output: Overdue commitment: Send the revised proposal to Alex Morgan. It was due Monday and is still open.
Upcoming recurring date: Northwind's annual renewal is on Friday.

output_examples.input: Check whether the two Sam Lee records should be merged.
output_examples.output: Both records share a name, but their verified emails and employers differ. No merge was made. Confirm which record you meant before making changes.

best_practices: Search by a stable identity and verify the matching profile before editing or merging.
Use external references for imported events and mark commitments resolved only after confirming the outcome.
Use a verified release and limit access to a dedicated CRM database. Share only the details needed for the task.
anti_patterns: Do not merge contacts based only on a shared name.
Do not invent historical events or inflate their significance to change relationship scores.
Do not export the entire database for a single contact review.

faq.question: What do I need to use Affinity?
faq.answer: Use a verified Affinity release with a CLI or local MCP connection. The release binary needs no separate runtime.

faq.question: Does Affinity use a cloud CRM?
faq.answer: Affinity stores records in local SQLite. Records returned to an AI assistant can enter its chat context, so limit what you retrieve.

faq.question: Can I use Affinity without changing records?
faq.answer: Yes. Search, review, and inspection are documented as read-only. Ask for an explicit read-only review before authorizing any changes.

faq.question: Can I import earlier conversations?
faq.answer: Yes. Import real events with known timestamps and use external references to prevent duplicate records when retrying.

faq.question: Will Affinity send birthday or renewal notifications?
faq.answer: Upcoming recurring dates appear in Affinity review views. Use a separate calendar or task tool for scheduled notifications.

faq.question: How do I handle a possible duplicate contact?
faq.answer: Inspect both records and compare their identities and histories. Merge only after confirming they represent the same contact and choosing which record to keep.
